ai.literal: Let one ask those worthy of being asked if seen; if they conceal, their blame, one's own blame is not.
ai.translation: You may ask for help if you find people worthy of being asked. If they refuse, the blame is theirs, not yours.
ai.modern: உதவி கேட்கத் தகுதியானவர்களைக் கண்டால் அவர்களிடம் உதவி கேட்கலாம். அவர்கள் உதவி செய்யாமல் மறைத்தால், அது அவர்களுக்குத்தான் பழியே தவிர, உதவி கேட்டவருக்குப் பழி இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the condition under which asking for help is acceptable. The word irattakkār refers to those who are generous and capable of giving. If one asks such worthy people and they refuse to give, the fault lies entirely with those who withheld their wealth. The act of asking the right person brings no shame to the one who asks.

ai.literal: joy to a person begging things begged for sorrow without experiencing if they come
ai.translation: Asking for help is a joy to a person, if the things asked for come without causing any sorrow.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் கேட்டுப் பெறும் பொருள்கள் அவருக்கு எந்தத் துன்பத்தையும் தராமல் மனமுவந்து அளிக்கப்படுமானால், அப்படிப் பிறரிடம் கேட்பது கூட அவருக்கு இன்பமானதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explores the rare condition under which asking for help can be considered pleasant. Generally, begging is seen as a source of humiliation and pain. However, if the things requested are given willingly and graciously, without causing any distress or loss of dignity to the receiver, then the very act of asking becomes a joy. The word 'உறாஅ' emphasizes that the transaction must be completely free of emotional or moral suffering.

ai.literal: Concealment without of heart duty knowers before standing, begging even a beauty possesses.
ai.translation: Standing before those who know their duty and have a heart that hides nothing, even begging possesses a certain beauty.
ai.modern: ஒளிவுமறைவு இல்லாத நெஞ்சமும், பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்கும் கடமையை அறிந்தவரும் ஆகிய சான்றோர் முன் நின்று ஒன்றை யாசிப்பதும் ஒரு அழகை உடையதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explores the rare circumstance where asking for help is not a source of shame. The word 'கரப்பு' means concealment, referring here to the act of hiding one's wealth to avoid giving. When one stands before noble people who know their duty ('கடன் அறிவார்') and have an open, generous heart ('கரப்பு இலா நெஞ்சின்'), the act of asking ('இரப்பு') loses its usual humiliation. In such a graceful exchange, even begging takes on a certain beauty ('ஏஎர் உடைத்து').

ai.translation: Begging is as joyful as giving itself, when asking from those who do not know how to withhold even in their dreams.

ai.explanation: This couplet elevates the act of asking for help when it is directed at the truly generous. The word 'karattal' means concealing or withholding what one has from those who ask. When one approaches people who do not even dream of withholding their wealth, the act of begging loses its usual sting. In such cases, asking brings as much joy and dignity as the act of giving itself.

Knowing that such open-hearted people exist, those in need are able to stand before them and undertake the act of asking for alms.

ai.literal: Concealment affliction those-without-(acc.) if-seen, poverty affliction all together will-perish.
ai.translation: If one sees those who do not have the affliction of hiding what they have, all the afflictions of poverty will perish at once.
ai.modern: தன்னிடம் உள்ளதை மறைத்து வைக்கும் நோய் இல்லாதவர்களைக் கண்டால், வறுமையால் வரும் துன்பங்கள் எல்லாம் ஒன்றாக அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts two types of suffering: the suffering of poverty and the suffering of stinginess. The word 'கரப்பு' means concealment, referring to the habit of hiding one's wealth to avoid giving to those who ask. The poet calls this an 'இடும்பை' (affliction), just as poverty ('நிரப்பு') is an affliction. When a person in need encounters someone free from the disease of withholding, all the sorrows of their poverty are destroyed at once.

ai.literal: Despising (and) without mocking, those who give (acc.) if seen, having rejoiced, mind inside-inside rejoicing it possesses.
ai.translation: If one sees those who give without scorn or mockery, the mind will rejoice and feel delight deep within.
ai.modern: தன்னை இகழ்ந்து ஏளனம் செய்யாமல் பொருள் கொடுப்பவரைக் கண்டால், இரப்பவரின் உள்ளம் மகிழ்ந்து தனக்குள்ளே பெருமகிழ்ச்சி அடையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the profound joy of a person in need when they encounter a truly gracious giver. The words 'இகழ்ந்து' (scorning) and 'எள்ளாது' (without mocking) highlight the usual humiliation associated with asking for help. In Tamil syntax, the negative in the second word applies to the first as well, meaning 'without scorning and mocking'. When a giver provides without this disdain, the receiver's reaction is not just relief, but deep emotional happiness. The repetition in 'உள்ளுள்' (deep within) emphasizes that this joy penetrates to the very core of their heart, restoring their dignity.

ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the social value of those who ask for help. Without beggars, the opportunity for charity and compassion would not exist. ai.literal: With those who give, what glory will exist, in the state of not having those who desire receiving by begging?
ai.translation: What glory would there be for givers, if there were no people willing to ask and receive?
ai.modern: இரந்து பெறுதலை விரும்புபவர்கள் இல்லாத நிலையில், கொடுப்பவர்களுக்கு என்ன பெருமை இருக்கும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the mutual relationship between the giver and the receiver. The word 'தோற்றம்' (appearance or glory) refers to the distinction and honor that philanthropists enjoy in society. However, this glory is entirely dependent on the existence of people who are in need and willing to beg ('இரந்துகோள் மேவார்'). Without receivers, the act of giving cannot happen, and thus the givers would have no opportunity to attain greatness.

ai.literal: He who begs not being angry is necessary; poverty's sorrow even itself is sufficient witness.
ai.translation: One who begs must not grow angry when refused. The sorrow of poverty itself is sufficient witness to the harshness of the world.
ai.modern: யாசிப்பவர் பிறர் பொருள் தர மறுக்கும்போது கோபப்படாமல் இருக்க வேண்டும். வறுமையால் வரும் துன்பமே அதற்குப் போதுமான சாட்சியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet instructs those who ask for help to refrain from anger when they are refused. The phrase 'vekuḷāmai vēṇṭum' clearly states that not getting angry is a necessity for a beggar. The second line explains that the sorrow of poverty ('nirappu iṭumpai') is itself a sufficient witness ('cālum kari'). This implies that the harsh suffering caused by poverty is proof enough of why others might cling to their wealth, making the beggar's anger both unjustified and futile.
